{{Quote|Is it a trap?''"<br />"''Of course.|Luke and Mara Jade Skywalker, upon discovery of Lumiya's datapad|<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Exile">''[[Legacy of the Force: Exile]]''</ref>}}
'''Lumiya's datapad''' was an electronic device utilized by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lady of the Sith]] during her preliminary instigations of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]. Well-hidden within [[Lumiya's second apartment|one]] of [[Apartment three hundred seven twelve|her many]] safe house apartments in the [[Zorp House]] complex on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] was discovered in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]] by [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Forces]] and members of the [[New Jedi Order|Jedi Order]] during an investigation into the [[Duel in the Fellowship Plaza|recent activities]] of [[Lumiya]]. Despite the lethality of the Dark [[Lord/Legends|Lady's]] trap-laden device, [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Mara Jade Skywalker]] was able to successfully bypass the safeguards and confiscate the datapad for future examination.

==Description==
{{Quote|That sounds like a small charge from someone as dedicated to overkill as she seems to be.''"<br />"''It is. That's because it's backed up by poison.|Luke and Mara Jade Skywalker discover the defense mechanisms|<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Exile" />}}
During her seduction of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lady of the Sith]] [[Lumiya]] made use of a specialized [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] with which she engaged in [[Spy/Legends|espionage]] as she manipulated the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|opposing]] [[Confederation|factions]] of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]. Lumiya modified her datapad to intercept communications within the [[Zorp House]] apartment complex of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]], as well as to [[Slicer/Legends|hack]] into the classified records of the [[Galactic Alliance Defense Force]]. The datapad included a self-replicating program that, left unchecked, would have eventually spread throughout the entirety of the military network. However, [[Galactic Alliance Intelligence Service|Galactic Alliance Intelligence]] [[operative]] [[Winter Celchu]] discovered and eradicated the malignant code. By all outward appearances, Lumiya's datapad was the same as any other commercially-available model. Countermeasures were installed to suit the Dark [[Lord/Legends|Lady's]] required anonymity, which included an explosives package situated near a smaller-than-standard [[Battery/Legends|battery]]. The explosives, which could destroy the datapad and disintegrate the [[Humanoid/Legends|handler's]] [[Limb/Legends|appendage]] in the process, also triggered the secondary trap: [[Trihexalon]] [[Poison/Legends|poison]], affixed beneath a thin layer of spray-on sealant.

Lumiya's datapad was spliced into one of a series of data cables just above a ceiling panel in a [[Lumiya's second apartment|secret apartment]] she kept in Zorp House. The [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|self-destruct mechanism]], which would also disperse the gaseous poison when activated, was rigged to breach the air duct it was located near, thereby spreading the Trihexalon throughout the building's ventilation system and exposing the entirety of its occupants to the [[Death/Legends|deadly]] toxin.

==History==
{{Quote|Our security has been compromised. An analysis of the data banks where that file was stored indicated that the only times it had been accessed in recent years was when automated backup programming refreshed it and compared it with static stored copies. Military programmers could find no other signs of intrusion, so I requested assistance from Intelligence, which revealed the method used&hellip;|[[General/Legends|General]] [[Tycho Celchu/Legends|Tycho Celchu]] discusses the existence of the code that originated from Lumiya's datapad|<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Exile" />}}
In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], Lumiya's secret apartment, and subsequently her datapad, were discovered by Zorp House's [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Zorp House building manager|maître d'hôtel]], who in turn contacted [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant's security force]]. Two detectives, accompanied by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] and [[Mara Jade Skywalker]], forced entry into Lumiya's apartment, where Jade Skywalker found the datapad as it had been left by the Neimoidian. She commenced to disassemble the device, during which [[Time/Legends|time]] she discovered and avoided the traps implemented by Lumiya. The [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] connected the datapad to one of her own and discovered the basic intercept-and-redirect algorithm programmed into the device. Once those present determined the start and end points of the transmissions, Jade Skywalker reattached the battery cover and secured the poison, explosives, and datapad, before they all departed in pursuit of the Dark Lady's trail.

==Behind the scenes==
Lumiya's datapad's first and only appearance took place in ''[[Legacy of the Force: Exile]]'', the fourth novel in the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'' series, written by [[Aaron Allston]]. In the abridged audio version of ''Exile'', narrated by [[Marc Thompson]], much of the detail regarding the datapad is omitted and is instead relegated to a fleeting mention in the audiobook's thirteenth chapter.
